questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cell junctions called tight, adhering and gap junctions are found in
questions.solution: All cells in the epithelium are held together with little intercellular material. In nearly all animal tissues, specialised junctions provide both structural and functional links between their individual cells. Three types of cell junctions are found in the epithelium and other tissues. These are called tight, adhering and gap junctions. Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Loose connective tissue has cells and fibres loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance, for example, areolar tissue present beneath the skin. Adipose tissue is a modified areolar tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialized to store fats. The excess of nutrients that are not used immediately are converted into fats and are stored in this tissue.

questions.solution: The cuboidal epithelium is composed of a single layer of cube-like cells. This is commonly found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons in kidneys and its main functions are secretion and absorption. The epithelium of proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron in the kidney has microvilli. Compound or stratified epithelium is made of more than one layer (multi-layered) of cells and their main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses. questions.solution:
The circulatory system of cockroach: It is of open type. Blood vessels are poorly developed and open into haemocoel or open spaces. Body fluid present in haemocoel is also known as haemolymph. Blood is colourless as there is no respiratory pigment. Blood doesn't perform the function of transporting gases. The circulatory system consists of heart, aorta, haemocoel and haemolymph. questions.q: The part of the sarcomere in which only myosin is present is termed as:
questions.solution:
I-band or Isotropic band or Light band: It contains actin.

A-band or Anisotropic band or Dark band: It contains myosin.

Z-line: It is an elastic fibre which passes through the centre of each I band and bisects it.

M line: It is a thin fibrous membrane which passes through the centre of each A band.

Sarcomere: It is the part of the myofibril between two successive Z lines. It is also considered as the functional unit of contraction.

H-zone: In a resting state, the ends of thin filaments on either side of the thick filaments partially overlap the free ends of the thick filaments, leaving the central part of the thick filaments. This central part of thick filament is not overlapped by thin filaments and is termed as H zone.

options: Spindle-shaped, unbranched, unstriated, uninucleate and involuntary
Spindle-shaped, unbranched, unstriped, multinucleate and involuntary
Cylindrical, unbranched, unstriped, multinucleate and involuntary
Cylindrical, unbranched, striated, multinucleate and involuntary
questions.solution:
Characteristics of smooth muscle fibres:
  • Cells range from 5 to 10 $\mu\text{m}$ in diameter and 30 to 200 $\mu\text{m}$ in length
  • Spindle-shaped
  • Single, centrally located nucleus.

Smooth muscle tissue occurs within almost every organ, forming sheets, bundles or sheaths around other tissues. Smooth muscle differs from both skeletal and cardiac muscle tissues in structure and function. Sarcomeres or myofibrils are not present (therefore not striated, i.e., smooth).

questions.solution: Ciliate Epithelium: Ciliated columnar epithelium is made of simple columnar epithelial cells with cilia on their free surfaces. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium. They are mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes. Microvilli are found on the free surface of columnar epithelium lining the alimentary canal to help increase surface area.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The largest part of the foregut of insects is ____ and is meant for ______.
questions.solution:
The foregut or stomodaeum of insects is lined by the cuticle. It consists of a buccal chamber, pharynx (short tubular), esophagus (narrow tubular), crop and gizzard.

Crop: It is a thin-walled, large-sized pear-shaped sac. It is the largest part of the foregut. It is meant for the storage of food.

Gizzard (or proventriculus): It is small but thick-walled. It is having a thick outer layer of circular muscles and thick inner cuticle with 6 highly chitinous plates known as teeth. It is meant for grinding and crushing of food.

questions.solution: The male& reproductive system consists of a pair of testes one lying on each lateral side in the 4th-6th abdominal segments. From each testis arises a thin vas deferens, which opens into the ejaculatory duct through seminal vesicle. The ejaculatory duct opens into male gonopore situated ventral to the anus. A characteristic mushroom-shaped gland is present in the 6th-7th abdominal segments which function as an accessory reproductive gland. The external genitalia is represented by male gonapophysis or phallomere (chitinous asymmetrical structures, surrounding the male gonopore).&

Body fluid present in haemocoel is also known as haemolymph. Blood is colourless as there is no respiratory pigment. Blood does not perform the function of transporting gases. Circulatory system consists of heart, aorta, haemocoel and haemolymph. The visceral organs bath in the fluid equivalent to blood in most invertebrates called hemolymph.

questions.solution: Cockroaches are brown or black bodied animals that are included in class Insecta of phylum Arthropoda. It has two types of wings. Forewings (mesothoracic) called tegmina are opaque dark and leathery and cover the hind wings when at rest. The hind wings are transparent, membranous and are used in flight. The mouthparts consisting of a labrum (upper lip), a pair of mandibles, a pair of maxillae and a labium (lower lip). A ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caeca is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice. With the help of several ommatidia, a cockroach can receive several images of an object. This kind of vision is known as a mosaic vision; it has more sensitivity but less resolution is common during the night.

questions.solution: Myofibrils are assembled of repeated structures called sarcomeres (the smallest functional unit of muscle fibre). However, a single muscle cell has many myofibril (muscle fibre) units. Each sarcomere is composed of actin (called thin) and myosin (called thick) filaments, arranged in a precise order, and protein complexes that support the filament structures.

Saliva, oil, digestive enzymes, thyroxine, FSH, mucus, insulin, earwax.
questions.solution:
On the basis of the mode of pouring of their secretions, glands are divided into two categories, namely, exocrine and endocrine glands. Exocrine glands secrete mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, digestive enzymes and other cell products. These products are released through ducts or tubes. In contrast, endocrine glands do not have ducts. Their products called hormones are secreted directly into the fluid, bathing the gland.
In the given list, insulin, FSH and thyroxine are hormones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: State the function of the gap junction found in the epithelium.
options: Performing the job of adhesion to keep neighbouring cells together.
Enabling relay of substances between adjoining cells by connecting cytoplasm for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules.
Not allowing the cells to come in contact with each other.
Preventing leakage of substances over and around tissue.
questions.solution:
Epithelial tissue are the type of tissue found in animal, which provide a lining or covering over other parts of the body. These tissues have certain connecting links, which give structural as well as functional support called as junctions. There are three types:
1. Tight junctions: They are present between cells. They support to prevent any leaks of material which is not required across the tissue and also in a way keep cells separate.
2. Adhering junctions: As the name suggests, they do the job of adhesion between cells, keeping it together.
3. Gap junctions: They are found in epithelial tissue and provide transport of material, viz., ions transport, small molecules, water etc., between adjacent cells.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: In nearly all animal tissues, specialised junctions provide both structural and functional links between their individual cells. Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The columnar epithelium is found in
questions.solution:
SIMPLE COLUMNAR EPITHELIUM:&
Structure: The cells of the simple columnar epithelium are tall pillar-like and are placed side by side. The free surface of columnar epithelial cells is smooth. The oval nucleus lies close to the base of the cell.
Location: Simple columnar epithelium forms a lining of the stomach, small intestine, colon, gall bladder, gastric glands, intestinal gland, and pancreatic lobules. Since here it performs the secretory functions, it is called the glandular epithelium. Certain cells of the columnar epithelium of stomach and intestine produce mucus which forms a fine mucus coating over epithelium. These mucus-producing cells are called goblet cells. The epithelium having mucus-secreting cells along with underlying connective-tissue is called mucous membrane or mucosa. The other columnar cells lining the intestine are specialized for the absorption of water and digested food. In order to surface area for absorption, they bear microvilli at the free ends. The columnar epithelium of this called brush-bordered columnar epithelium.
Function: Protection, secretion, and absorption.

questions.q: The tissue with the power of division and regeneration, throughout life, is _________.
questions.solution: Epithelial tissue covers the outside of the body and lines organ cavities. The tissue always rests upon underlying connective tissue and are closely packed with each other so there is very little intercellular space. Due to absence/less of intercellular spaces, blood vessels, lymph vessels and capillaries are unable to pierce this tissue so blood circulation is absent in epithelium. Hence cells depend on their nutrients on underlying connective tissue. The cells of this tissue can divide throughout life with high regeneration capacity as they process the stem cells.

The heart is divided into 13 funnel-shaped chambers, of which 3 lie in the thorax and 10 in the abdomen. Each chamber has a pair of openings at the sides called ostia. The ostia are guarded by valves which allow the flow of blood from pericardial sinus in to the heart but not in the opposite direction. During circulation blood flow in to the heart through ostia. The heart chambers contract one after the other rapidly and it is due to contraction and relaxation of alary muscles. This pushes the blood into the anterior aorta i.e. the anterior-most heart chamber. From aorta, the blood passes in the head sinus and into other sinuses. All the chambers of heart are interconnected and their openings is guarded by valves to maintain unidirection flow of blood.

The genital pouch of female cockroach is made up of two parts. The anterior small part and posterior large part. Anterior part is known as genital chamber and posterior part is known as oothecal chamber or vestibulum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following tissue is possessed by a blue whale which lies beneath the skin and helps during hibernation?
questions.solution: Blue whale possess a special tissue - which lies beneath the skin and helps during hibernation Hibernators depend on their fat reserves while cold and to fuel rewarming.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
A student was given a sample of tissue. He observes and concludes the following characters.

(i) The cells are composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells.

(ii) Their nuclei are located at the base.

(iii) Free surface may have microvilli.

(iv) It is found in the lining of stomach and intestine.

(v) It helps in secretion and absorption.

Based on the above features identify the epithelium.
questions.solution: The epithelium is a protective tissue of animals. It is divided into simple and compound epithelium on the basis of layers resting on the basement membrane. The simple epithelium consists of only one layer. This epithelium is further divided into various types depending on the shape of cells. These are squamous epithelium, cuboidal epithelium, columnar epithelium, ciliated epithelium and pseudostratified epithelium. Columnar epithelium consists of tall or pillar like cells in which length is more than the width and so nuclei appear to be located at the base of cells. This epithelium causes absorption and secretion and to increase the surface area this epithelium also shows the presence of microvilli. This is known as brush bordered epithelium. The columnar epithelium is found in the lining of stomach and intestine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statement is true about cockroach?
options: There are three ganglia in thorax and nine in abdomen
Each eye consists of about 6000 hexagonal ommatidia
Fat body, nephrocytes and uricose glands help in excretion
Respiratory system consists of network of trachea that open through 8 pairs of spiracles
questions.solution: Cockroaches consist of nine ganglia. Out of these three are present in the thorax and six are in the abdomen. Cockroaches consist of compound eyes and these contain small units known as ommatidia. which is around 2000 in number. Respiratory system consists of ten pairs of spiracles. Excretion is done with the help of Fat bodies, nephrocytes and uricose glands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following tissue exerts the greatest control over the body's responsiveness to changing conditions?
questions.solution: Neural tissue exerts the greatest control over the body's responsiveness to changing conditions. The neuron and neuroglial cells of this tissue can control and co-ordinate the all activities of human body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Simple epithelium is a tissue in which the cells are
options: hardened and provide support to the organs.
cemented directly to one another to form a single layer.
continuously dividing to provide form to an organ.
loosely connected to one other to form an irregular organ.
questions.solution: Simple epithelium is a tissue made of a single layer of compactly arranged cells all of which rest over a noncellular basement membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement about cockroaches from the following.
options: Antennae have sensory receptors that help in monitoring the environment.&
The head is formed by the fusion of six segments and shows great mobility in all directions due to flexible neck.
The first pair of wings arise from the mesothorax and the second pair from the metathorax.
In males, the genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of abdomen bounded ventrally by 9th and 10th terga and dorsally by the 9th sternum.
questions.solution: The abdomen in both males and females consists of 10 segments. In females, the 7th sternum is boat shaped and together with the 8th and 9th sterna forms a brood or genital pouch whose anterior part contains female gonopore, spermathecal pores and collateral glands. In males, genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of abdomen bounded dorsally by 9th and 10th terga and ventrally by the 9th sternum. It contains dorsal anus, ventral male genital pore and gonapophysis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: All of the following structure in a cockroach has jointed segmental or filamentous structure except;
questions.solution: In male cockroach a pair of short, sensitive, unjointed, and thread-like structures called anal style is present. This structure helps in the process of copulation. Antenna, anal cerci and walking legs are all jointed segmental or filamentous structures.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the correct match from the following.
questions.solution: Loose connective tissue has cells and fibres loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance, for example, areolar tissue present beneath the skin. Often it serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibres), macrophages and mast cells.&

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following specialized connective tissues intercellular material is solid, pliable, and resists compression?
questions.solution: The specialized connective tissue, the cartilage that is solid, pliable, and resists compression. Cartilage is made up of specialized cells called chondrocytes which produces a large amount of collagenous extracellular matrix and ground substance that is rich in proteoglycan and elastin fibers.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
How many of the following statements is/are correct?

(i) Multipolar neurons are found in the cerebral cortex.
(ii) Unipolar neurons have a cell body with one axon only.
(iii) The myelinated nerve fibres are enveloped with Schwann cells.
(iv) The postsynaptic neurons are filled with neurotransmitter containing vesicles.
questions.solution: The postsynaptic neurons have receptors for the neurotransmitters. The presynaptic neurons contain neurotransmitter containing vesicles and have mitochondria.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Recognise the figure and find out the CORRECT matching.
options: a - forewing, b - anal style, c - mesothorax, d - prothorax, e - tegmina

a - tegmina, b - anal cerci, c - mesothorax d - pronotum, e - hind wing

questions.solution: Cockroaches belong to Phylum Arthropoda. The body is divided into Head, Thorax and Abdomen. Thorax is divided into three parts: Prothorax, Mesothorax and Metathorax. Prothorax has largest tergem and this is known as Pronotum. Thorax also shows presence of appendages and wings. Thorax shows three pairs of appendages attached to each part of thorax. Two pairs of wings attached are forewings and hindwings. Forewings are covered with thick sheet known as tegmina. Male and female cockroaches show presence of anal cerci which are abdominal appendages.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Refer to the characteristics given below and identify how many are true for a skeletal muscle?

Uninucleated, branched, dark and light band, actin and myosin filaments, spindle-shaped cells
questions.solution: Skeletal muscles are also called striated or voluntary muscles. Striated muscles are attached to bones by tendons. They have long, thin, multinucleated fibres having alternate light and dark band (striations). They contain myofibrils which contain contractile proteins thin actin and thick myosin. Smooth muscle cells are uninucleate, spindle shape and don't have any striations. Cardiac muscle cells are uninucleate, show faint striations and are branched cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these statements about sphincters of urethra is CORRECT?
options: Internal urethral sphincter is made up of smooth muscles while external urethral sphincter is made up of striated muscles.
Internal urethral sphincter is made up of striated muscles while external urethral sphincter is made up of smooth muscles.
Both internal and external urethral sphincter is made up of smooth muscles.
Both internali and external urethral sphincter is made up of striated muscles.
questions.solution: The human excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra. The urethra is the opening through which urine gets released out of the body. It is of different lengths in males and females. It is around 20 cm in males and 4 cm in females. It shows the presence of two sphincters that control the flow of urine. These are internal and external sphincters (sphincters are openings made up of circular muscles). The internal sphincter is involuntary as it is made up of smooth muscles while external sphincters are voluntary as it is made up of skeletal muscles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The ventral diaphragm of cockroach is present in between
questions.solution: The body of the cockroach is divided into three sinuses. Pericardial on the dorsal side, perineural on the ventral side and perivisceral in the center. Two diaphragms separate these three sinuses. The ventral diaphragm is between perivisceral and perineural sinuses and the dorsal diaphragm is between pericardial and perivisceral sinuses. There is ostia present, which acts as communication between these sinuses.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is also called modified areolar tissue?
questions.solution: Loose connective tissue (Cell and fibres are loosely arranged in a semi –fluid ground substance) $1.$ Areolar tissue : It possess fibroblast cells, mast cells and macrophages. It act as supporting framework for epithelia. $2.$ Adipose tissue : This tissue is modified for storing fats. Excess of nutrients are converted to fats and stored in it. Location : Adipose tissue layer beneath the skin as panniculus adiposus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The matrix of bone is hard due to __A__ while that of cartilage is pliable due to __B__
options:
A B
Calcium salts Hyaluronic acid A

questions.solution: Bone and cartilage both are specialized structural connective tissue. Cartilage is pliable and in embryonic life, this undergoes ossification to form bones. This formation is known as endochondrial ossification. After this ossification, some amount of cartilage persists and hence it is seen covering the bones. Cartilage forms bone by deposition of calcium and hence cartilage when it gets calcified into the bone. The matrix of cartilage consists of chondrin protein and chondroitin salts instead of calcium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the number of chambers in the heart of Periplaneta americana?
questions.solution:
The circulatory system of cockroach:

- It is an open type. Blood vessels are poorly developed and open into haemocoel or open spaces.

- Body fluid present in hemocoel is also known as hemolymph.

- Blood is colorless as there is no respiratory pigment.

- Blood doesn't perform the function of transporting gases.

- Cockroach possesses 13- chambered tubular, muscular, elongated and neurogenic heart.

- Blood circulation in cockroach is maintained by wing-shaped alary muscles (involuntary).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about skeletal muscles?
options: They are under the direct control of ANS.
They are primarily found in hollow organs.
They are bundled together in a parallel fashion.
questions.solution:
Characteristics of skeletal muscles:

- These are closely associated with the skeletal components of the body.
- In a typical muscle such as the biceps, striated (striped) skeletal muscle fibres are bundled together in a parallel fashion. A sheath of tough connective tissue encloses several bundles of muscle fibres.
- A type of striated muscles (have striped appearance under the microscope)
- These are primarily involved in locomotory actions and changes of body postures.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following structure is connected with double ventral nerve cord in Periplaneta americana?
questions.solution: In Cockroach, the brain is represented by Supra-oesophageal ganglion whereas from Sub-oesophageal ganglion double ventral nerve cord originates having nine segmentally arranged ganglia arise on ventral side of thorax and abdomen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements and mark the incorrect statement regarding cardiac muscle.
options: It is a contractile tissue present in heart
They are not under the control of will of the animals
questions.solution: The muscles in our body are divided into three groups: Skeletal muscles, Smooth muscles and Cardiac muscles. Skeletal muscles are voluntary and striated. Smooth muscles are involuntary and non striated. Cardiac muscles are related to heart. These are structurally similar to skeletal muscles but functionally similar to smooth muscles. Structural similarities include presence of striations and peripheral nuclei. Similarities between smooth and cardiac muscles is both are involuntary and show uninucleate fibres.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the correct statement about a cockroach.
options: The sclerites are joined to each other by a thick, hard and non-flexible arthrodial membrane.
Each thoracic segments bears a pair of flying wings.
In the cockroach, the fat body, nephrocytes and urecose glands helps in excretion.
A characteristic mushroom gland is present in the 4-6^{th} abdominal segments.
questions.solution: The sclerites are joined to each other by a thin and flexible arthrodial membrane. Each thoracic segments bears a pair of walking legs. A characteristic mushroom gland is present in the 6-7^{th} abdominal segments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The tissue lining the inner surface of a hollow organ like a fallopian tube is:
questions.solution: The inner surface of hollow visceral organs like bronchioles, fallopian tube and ventricles of brain are lined by ciliated columnar epithelium. The function of cilia is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the option which gives the correct information about the white muscle fiber.

The amount of endoplasmic reticulum is high and the number of mitochondria is also high
The amount of endoplasmic reticulum is low and the number of mitochondria is high
The amount of endoplasmic reticulum is low and the number of mitochondria is low
questions.solution:
White muscle fibres:

$1.$ These have a very less quantity of myoglobin, giving them whitish (or pale) appearance.

$2.$ The number of mitochondria are very few.

$3.$ These muscles are also known as anaerobic muscles as these depend on anaerobic process for energy.

$4.$& The amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum is high.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In which of the following tissue, cells of the tissue are enclosed in small cavities within the solid and pliable matrix secreted by them?
questions.solution: Intercellular material is solid, pliable and incompressible. Matrix is having small cavities in which chondrocytes (cells) are present. Occurrence: During embryonic stages, most of the endoskeleton was made up of cartilage which is gradually replaced by bones. Other sites: Tip of nose, outer ear joints, between vertebra, limbs and hands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the statements which are incorrect.

$\left(a\right)$ Blood cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.
$\left(b\right)$ Neuroglial cells protect and support the nephrons.
$\left(c\right)$ Osteocytes are present in spaces called lacunae.
$\left(d\right)$ Striated muscle fibres are bundled together in a parallel fashion.
$\left(e\right)$ Biceps are involuntary and striated.
questions.solution: Blood is a specialized fluid connective tissue as it lacks fibres. Neuroglial cells are supporting cells of nervous system and forms more than half of total cells in this system. Osteocytes and Chondrocytes are present in spaces known as lacunae and these are present in the matrix. Lacunae of osteocytes also show presence of canaliculi which is absent in lacunae of chondrocytes. Striated muscle bundles are not in parallel fashion. Biceps are skeletal muscles and hence show striations and are voluntary in function.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not a part of the respiratory system of Periplaneta americana?
questions.solution:
Respiratory system (tracheal system). It is well-developed and consists of:

$1.$ Network of trachea. $2.$ Tracheoles (thin branching tubes) $3.$ Spiracles (10 pairs).

Trachea forms a network and its branches reach to every part of the body without involving the circulatory system. Body tissues receive the oxygen by diffusion from the tracheoles.

Spiracles are equivalent to the nostrils of the human through which the tracheal system open outside to atmosphere. First thoracic and abdominal spiracles remain always open while other are guarded by sphincters or valves. Sclerites are chitinous plates covering the segments - 2 pleurites (lateral), 1 tergite (dorsal) and 1 sternite (ventral). These sclerites are joined together by arthrodial membrane which is a thin and flexible articular membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements and find out the INCORRECT statement.
options: In cockroach, brain supplies nerves to antennae and compound eyes.
Fat body, nephrocytes and uricose glands also helps in excretion in cockroach.

Male cockroach bears one ootheca that is a dark reddish to
blackish brown capsule, about 3/8" (8 mm) long.
questions.solution: Cockroaches belong to phylum Arthropoda and class Insecta. The body is divided into head, thorax, and abdomen. Head bears compound eyes that are responsible for mosaic vision because each eye has many lenses. The brain is in the form of ganglia and nerves arise from these ganglia to supply eyes and antennae. Nephrocytes are major structures for excretion. Fat bodies and uricose glands in males are also for the same function. The ootheca& is a dark reddish to blackish brown capsule, about 3/8" (8 mm) long in female reproductive structure, where the collateral glands secrete oothecal cover.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the one common feature found in all types of connective tissues despite their variation in different aspects?
questions.solution: There are four types of animal tissues: Epithelial tissue, Connective tissue, Muscular tissue and Nervous tissue. Connective tissue is the most abundant animal tissue. It is further divided into Lose Connective tissue, Dense Connective tissue and Specialised Tissue. All these types are very different in structure and function but have certain common features. The main feature common to all connective tissue is presence of Matrix. This is seen only in this tissue. It consists of cells and sometimes fibres too.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following structures in Periplaneta is correctly matched with its function?
options: Supra-oesophageal ganglion - Supplies nerves to antennae
questions.solution:
In the head region, the brain is represented by supra oesophageal ganglion which supplies nerves to antennae and compound eyes.

A ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caeca is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, which secrete
digestive juice.

Heart is attached to the body wall by 12 pairs of alary muscles.& The heart chambers contract one after the other rapidly and it is due to contraction and relaxation of alary muscles.

There is a pair of spermathecae opening in to the genital pouch in the 6^{th} abdominal segment of female cockroach. This is filled with sperms after copulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not a connection between the plasma membrane of adjacent cells?
questions.solution: Desmosomes are intercellular junctions which provide strong bond between cells. They join intermediate filaments of neighbouring cells. Tight junctions between cells are nothing but connected areas of the plasma membrane that stitch cells together. Gap junctions directly connect the cytoplasm of two cells allowing molecules and ions to directly pass through.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is an abundant connective tissue of body?
questions.solution: Areolar connective tissue is a type of connective tissue consisting of a matrix, protein fibres (collagen and elastin) and such cells as fibroblasts, mast cells, macrophages, and fat cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following feature is not applicable for red muscle fibres?
options: It has high content of red colour oxygen storing pigment myoglobin.
It also contain plenty of mitochondria for maximum ATP production.
It has also high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
It is also called as aerobic muscles.
questions.solution: Red muscle fibres are aerobic muscle fibres with high amount of myoglobin, plenty of mitochondria which can utilise the large amount of oxygen stored in them for ATP production. These muscle fibres has low amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mark the INCORRECT statement regarding connective tissue.
options: Most abundant and widely distributed body tissue
questions.solution: Connective tissues arise from mesenchyme - an embryonic tissue which in turn arises from mesoderm, an embryonic germ layer. Cells of connective tissues secrete collagen and elastin fibres. They help in connecting, binding and supporting different structures of the animal body. Ligaments connect the bone to muscles whereas tendon connects bone to bone. They are highly vascular in nature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Peritoneum of coelom is an example of
questions.solution: Epithelial tissue can be classified as simple or compound epithelium depending on the number of layers resting on the basement membrane. The simple epithelium consists of only one layer resting on the basement membrane. This is further divided into various types depending on the shape of cells. These are squamous epithelium when the cells are flat, cuboidal when the cells are square in shape, columnar when the cells are tall and pillar like and ciliated when cells show the presence of cilia. The main function of simple epithelium is the transport of substances. Peritoneum shows flat cells and hence is an example of simple squamous epithelium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is INCORRECT about a cockroach?
options: In females, a pair of spermatheca is present in the 6^{th} segment which opens into the genital chamber.
Male genital pouch is present dorsal to anus and contain male genital pore and gonapophysis.
The heart is differentiated into funnel shaped chambers with ostia on either side.
Blood vascular system is open type in which blood from sinuses enter heart through ostia and pumped anteriorly.
questions.solution: Cockroaches are brown/black bodied animals from class Insecta of Phylum Arthropoda. They have well developed reproductive organs in both sexes. Male reproductive system consists of a pair of testes on each lateral side. From each testis arises a thin vas deferens, which opens into ejaculatory duct through seminal vesicle that opens into male gonopore situated ventral to anus. The genetelia are external and represented by male gonapophysis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the INCORRECT statement in reference to the unstriated muscles.
options: Their contractions are under the control of autonomous nervous system
They lack actin and myosin proteins, hence lack striations
They possess uninucleated, fusiform-shaped cells which taper at both the ends
questions.solution: There are three types of muscle groups seen in humans. Skeletal or striated muscles, smooth or unstriated muscles, and cardiac muscles. Unstriated muscles are so named because these muscles lack striations i.e. dark and light bands. Hence these are smooth muscles. These muscles are not under our control and hence are also known as involuntary muscles. These muscles are present lining the internal organs and hence are visceral muscles. These are under the control of the autonomic nervous system. The muscle fibres are fusiform shaped that taper at both the ends and are uninucleated. Cell junctions are seen in between the fibres.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The blood stem cells are related to which among the following options
questions.solution: Bone marrow is a soft and spongy tissue present inside the bones. These tissues make blood-forming cells or blood stem cells. White blood cells to fight infections, red blood cells to carry oxygen throughout the body, platelets to control bleeding, macrophages for phagocytic functions are all produced in these tissues.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following epithelium is most suitable for the quick& exchange of materials& through membranes via filtration or diffusion?
questions.solution: Simple squamous epithelia consist of a single layer of flattened cells in contact with the basal lamina. This type of epithelial lines the inner surface of all blood vessels (endothelium), forms the wall of alveolar sacs in the lung and lines the body cavities (mesothelium). This type of epithelium is often permeable and occurs where small molecules need to pass quickly through membranes via filtration or diffusion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: All of the following can be found in the female cockroach, except
questions.solution:
Female cockroach differs from the male cockroach in may features -

- The body of male cockroach is relatively smaller than the female cockroach

- The antennae of female is larger than in males.

- Boat shaped abdomen is present in female cockroach and its last segment is blunt.

- The wing size of female cockroach is not as large as that of the males and extend up to the tip of the abdomen.

- The 10th segment bears a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci found in both sexes and the males bear a thread like small structure called as anal styles (caudal style). This is absent in the female.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If a cell receives a signal to contract, then its neighbours are also stimulated to contract. This is due to the presence of -
questions.solution: Unique junctions called intercalated discs (communication junctions) link the cells together and define their borders. Intercalated discs are the major portal for cardiac cell-to-cell communication, which is required for coordinated muscle contraction and maintenance of circulation.& Communication junctions at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit, i.e., when one cell receives a signal to contract, its neighbours are also stimulated to contract.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Find out the CORRECT statement.
options: Ciliated epithelium present in convoluted parts of nephric tubule absorb only water.
Haversian canals are interconnected by canaliculi and lacunae.
Abdominal wall in our body has striated involuntary muscles.
Elastic cartilage is present in the tip of our nose
questions.solution:
Bone is a rigid connective tissue forming an integral part of the endoskeleton in vertebrates. There are many minute column-like structures present in it namely the Haversian system. These contain layers of bone cells around a central canal called Haversian canal. These columns are connected to each other by perforating channels- Volkmann's canal.

Cartilage is a type of connective tissue forming soft boy structures of nose tip, ear pinna. Nose tip contain hyaline cartilage whereas the ear pinna has elastic cartilage.

Simple cuboidal epithelium is found in the convoluted parts of nephron that help in water absorption. Ciliated epithelium is found in the inner walls of trachea and even in the fallopian tube of female reproductive system.

The abdominal wall of the body has skeletal muscles as there is voluntary control over the movement. Smooth muscles are found in the alimentary canal of the body.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Cockroaches belong to Phylum Arthropoda. The body is divided into head, thorax, and abdomen. Head bears compound eyes. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the given statements about the blood vascular system of cockroach.

I. The circulatory system of cockroach is of closed type
II. It contains no blood vessels except aorta of the heart.
III. The heart is 6-chambered.
IV. The haemolymph is composed of colourless plasma and haemocytes.

Which of the statement(s) given above is/are INCORRECT?
questions.solution: Cockroaches belong to Phylum Arthropods. These show open type of circulation as proper system of blood vessels and heart is not seen. Circulation is through open sinuses. Only one blood vessel is seen i.e. Aorta in the head region. Heart in cockroaches are on the dorsal side and consists of 13 chambers. The circulatory fluid is haemolymph that consists of colourless plasma and haemocytes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following characteristics is correct for epithelial tissues?
options: The cells are compactly packed with fluid intercellular matrix
The cells are loosely packed with abundant intercellular matrix
The cells are compactly packed with little or no intercellular matrix
The cells are loosely packed with little intercellular matrix
questions.solution: Epithelial tissues are the major tissue in glands and form the outer covering or layer of all body surfaces and organs. It consists of closely aggregated cells that adhere firmly to each other and forming either single or multiple layers. Due to the cells being tightly packed there is the very little intercellular matrix. The intercellular matrix consists of protein and is on the cell membrane of epithelial cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
From the given list, how many are unpaired structures of a cockroach?

Tergites, Labium, Hypopharynx, Tegmina, Genital pouch, Labrum, Mandible
questions.solution: The cockroach has a segmented body and is divided into head, thorax and abdomen. There is a pair of antennae arising from the sockets in front of the eyes. The labrum and the labium are the upper and lower lip with a hypopharynx which is the tongue. The tergites are the hardened dorsal plates of the exoskeleton and the genital pouch is a part of the female cockroach formed by the 8th and 9th sterna. Therefore the cockroaches have only two paired structures which are its forewings(tegmina) and the mandibles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Gap junctions are present in:
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Gap junctions facilitate rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules between adjoining cells. Gap junctions are present in epithelial tissue, cardiac tissue and single unit smooth muscles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Brood pouch in female Periplaneta americana is composed of:
questions.solution: All part of the female reproductive systems is confined to the abdomen region. These include a pair of ovaries, a pair of oviducts, spermathecae, collateral glands, genital pouch and external genitalia. Genital pouch is also known as a brood pouch. It is formed by contribution of 7^{th}, 8^{th&}and 9^{th}& sternum. 7^{th}& sternum is large and boat shaped. The pouch is divided into two parts: small anterior and large posterior. Small anterior is known as genital atrium and large is vestibulum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What external changes are visible after the last moulting of a cockroach nymph?
options: Both fore wings and hind wings develop
questions.solution: Cockroaches show paurometabolous development. This is gradual metamorphosis. In this type the young ones resemble adults and have wings attached to the body. The young forms are known as nymphs. The nymph undergoes 13 times moulting to form adults. & The next to last nymphal stage has wing pads but only adult cockroaches have wings. Thus, the nymph after the last moulting bears both forewings and hind wings.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The connective tissue having the presence of abundant fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells is:
options:
Type of connective tissue Location
Adipose tissue Beneath the skin

Type of connective tissue Location
Areolar tissue Beneath the skin

Type of connective tissue Example
Dense connective tissue Tendons

Type of connective tissue Location
Specialised connective tissue Cartilage
questions.solution: Areolar connective tissue: A type of connective tissue consisting of a gel-like matrix incorporating strands of protein fibres (collagen and elastin) and such cells as fibroblasts, mast cells, macrophages, and fat cells. This tissue is found throughout the body under the skin and linking organs and other tissues.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Components of the areolar connective tissue include all of the following, except
questions.solution:
Loose connective tissue has cells and fibres loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance, for example, areolar tissue present beneath the skin. Often it serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibres), macrophages and mast cells. Collagen or elastin fibres along with a semi-fluid ground substance called the matrix is found all connective tissues.
Chondrocytes or cartilage cells comprise the intercellular material of cartilage, which is solid and pliable and resists compression.& These cells are enclosed in small cavities within the matrix secreted by them.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following cell junctions is highly permeable and cause easy passage of substance across the cell membranes?
questions.solution: Gap junctions are aggregates of intercellular channels that permit direct cell-cell transfer of ions and small molecules.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is INCORRECT for forewings of a cockroach?
options: Also called mesothoracic wings or tegmina
Cover the hind wings when at rest
questions.solution: The body of cockroach is divided into head, thorax, and abdomen. Head bears compound eyes, mouthparts, and antennae. Thorax is divided into three parts: the prothorax, mesothorax, and metathorax. Three pairs of legs and two pairs of wings arise from the thorax. Each pair arises from each part of the thorax and thus these are named as prothorax, mesothoracic and metathoracic legs. The two pairs of wings are forewings and hindwings. Forewings arise from the mesothorax or junction of pro and mesothorax. Hence, these wings are known as mesothoracic wings. These are covered by a thick sheath known as tegmina. These being thick cannot be used for flying and hence are used to protect the delicate hind wings while walking. Hind wings are used in flight.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which part of the alimentary canal of cockroach has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth?
questions.solution: The alimentary canal in cockroaches is divided into three parts: foregut, midgut, and hindgut. Foregut consists of mouth, esophagus, crop, and gizzard. The crop is the largest part of the foregut. Its main function is to store food. The gizzard is also known as proventriculus. Food from crop enters the gizzard. The gizzard is made up of muscles and also consists of teeth in the inner layer and thus it helps in grinding. Food from the gizzard then enters the midgut where remaining grinding and absorption takes place.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Sebaceous glands eliminate certain substances like _____________through sebum.
questions.solution: Sebaceous glands are oil glands present in the skin. These act as accessory excretory organs. These eliminate substances like sterols, hydrocarbons and waxes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cells of the main structural tissue of the body are present in particular spaces called
questions.solution: Bones have a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres which give bone its strength. It is the main tissue that provides the structural frame to the body. Bones support and protect softer tissues and organs. The bone cells (osteocytes) are present in the spaces called lacunae. These lacunae also have extensions known as canaliculi. Lacunae are present in the matrix of cartilage too but are without canaliculi.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Smooth muscles are
questions.solution: Muscles are classified as Skeletal, Smooth and Cardiac muscles depending on structure, position and function.Skeletal muscles are voluntary muscles. These are also known as striated or striped muscles due to presence of striations. Smooth muscles are involuntary in function. These are also known as visceral muscles due to its location around internal organs. These are non striated muscles. The muscle fibres are spindle shaped i.e. tapering at both the ends and are uninucleate.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A female cockroach can be differentiated from a male cockroach, due to the presence of:
questions.solution:
Male cockroach bears a pair of short, thread-like structure in 9^{th} abdominal segment called anal style. In both sexes, the 10^{th&}abdominal segment bears a pair of a jointed filamentous structure called anal cerci.

In females, the 7^{th} sternum is boat shaped and together with the 8^{th} and 9^{th&}sterna forms a brood or genital pouch whose anterior part contains female gonopore, spermathecal pores and collateral glands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The tissue whose cells acts like a diffusion boundary is:
questions.solution: The squamous epithelium is made up of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. They are found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs and are involved in functions like forming diffusion boundary for efficient diffusion process.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements about the cockroach and select the option:

I. Forewings (mesothoracic) called tegmina are opaque dark and leathery and cover the hind wings.
II. Head is formed by the fusion of eight segments and shows little mobility.
III. Genital pouch in male is formed by 9^{th} and 10^{th} terga and 9^{th} sternum.
options: I, II and III are correct
questions.solution:
Head is triangular in shape and lies anteriorly at right angles to the longitudinal body axis. It is formed by the fusion of six segments and shows great mobility in all directions due to flexible neck.

The first pair of wings arises from mesothorax and the second pair from metathorax. Forewings (mesothoracic) called tegmina are opaque dark and leathery and cover the hind wings when at rest. The hind wings are transparent, membranous and are used in flight.

In males, genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of abdomen bounded dorsally by 9^{th} and 10^{th} terga and ventrally by the 9^{th} sternum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is incorrect regarding compound epithelium?
options: Cover the moist surface of buccal cavity and pharynx.
Provide protection against chemical and mechanical stress.
Thy play a vital role in secretion and absorption.
questions.solution: The compound epithelium is made of more than one layer (multi-layered) of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption.& Their main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses. They cover the dry surface of the skin, the moist surface of the buccal cavity, pharynx, the inner lining of ducts of salivary glands and of pancreatic ducts.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statement and choose the CORRECT option.
options: Blood cells secrete fibers of structural protein called collagen
Osteocytes are present in fluid filled cavity called Lamellae
questions.solution: Blood and Lymph are fluid connective tissue. These tissues do not have fibres and thus collagen or elastin are also absent. Osteocytes are bone forming cells. These are present in a bone cavity called Lacunae that also has extensions known as canaliculi. Lamellae are concentric layers of compact bone surrounding the haversian canal in mammals. Striated fibres are unbranched and show striations. Basophils are Granulocytes. These are types of Leukocytes. These are $0 - 1%$ of the total WBC's. These secrete substances like Histamine, Serotonin and heparin. Histamine is a Vasodilator. Serotonin mainly acts as Vasoconstrictor while Heparin is an anticoagulant. Thus basophils are non-phagocytic.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the following with reference to cockroach and choose the CORRECT option.
&
& Column I & Column II
P. Anal style (i) $10th$ tergite
Q. Testis (ii) ${2}^{nd}$ - $6th$ segments
R. Anal cerci (iii) $9th$ stemite
S. Ovary (iv) $4th$ - $6th$
questions.solution:
In cockroaches, the male reproductive system consists of a pair of testes, vas deferns, ejaculatory duct, seminal vesicle, mushroom gland and external genitalia. Testes are present at 4^{th} to 6^{th} segments.

The female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries, oviduct, vagina, genital chamber. Ovaries are present at 2^{nd} to 6^{th} segments.

Male and female cockroaches show sexual dimorphism. Males show presence of anal cerci and anal styles while females have only anal cerci. Anal cerci arises from 10^{th} tergite and anal style is from 9^{th} sternite.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is correct for the circulatory system of cockroach?
options: It is present on the dorsal side and it has thirteen units of heart in abdominal region
It is present on the ventral side and it has ten abdominal and three thoracic units of heart
It is present on the ventral side and it has thirteen units of heart in abdominal region
It is present on the dorsal side and it has ten abdominal and three thoracic units of heart
questions.solution: Heart of cockroach is a dorsal, pulsatile 13 chambered (ten abdominal and three thoracic chambers) structure. This heart is, infact the dorsal blood vessel, which pulsates, with the help of external alary muscles, that's why it is also called as myogenic heart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Arrange the following structures according to their decreasing number.

Hepatic or gastric caeca ; Malpighian tubules ; Ommatidia
questions.solution:
Hepatic caeca are 6 to 8 blind tubules present at the junction of foregut and midgut.

At the junction of midgut and hindgut 100 to 150 yellow coloured thin filaments malpighian tubules are present.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the correct option:

I. In the skeletal muscle fibre, a large number of myofilaments are arranged in the sarcoplasm.
II. The central part of an anisotropic band where the only thick filament is present and thin filament is absent is called 'A' band.
III. In the resting state, a tropomyosin protein masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
IV. The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called motor-end plate.
options: I, II and IV are true
II, III and IV are true
questions.solution:
The light bands contain actin and is called I-band or Isotropic band, whereas the dark band called ‘A’ or Anisotropic band contains myosin. Both the proteins are arranged as rod-like structures, parallel to each other and also to the longitudinal axis of the myofibrils. Actin filaments are thinner as compared to the myosin filaments, hence are commonly called thin and thick filaments respectively.&
The central part of anisotropic or A band where only thick or myosin filament is present and thin or actin filament is absent is called 'H' zone. In the middle of this zone a thin fibrous membrane 'M' line is present.& In a resting state, the edges of thin filaments on either side of the thick filaments partially overlap the free ends of the thick filaments leaving the central part of the thick filaments. The H zone is not overlapped by the thin filaments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following and select the only true statements about cockroach:

$A.$ Each Malpighian tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells.
$B.$ A characteristic mushroom gland is present in the female cockroach in the 6th-7th abdominal segments.
$C.$ Both compound eye consists of about 2000 hexagonal ommatidia.
$D.$ The development of P. americana is paurometabolous through the nymphal stage.
questions.solution: A characteristic mushroom gland is present in male cockroach only in the 6th-7th abdominal segments. It functions as an accessory reproductive gland. Both compound eye consists of about 4000 hexagonal ommatidia.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the incorrect statement regarding animal tissue?
options: Epithelial cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix.
Tight junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.
Connective tissue ranges from very soft to very hard specialised types.
Cell junctions hold smooth muscle fibres together and are covered by connective tissue sheath.
questions.solution:
Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. These junctions are usually found in apical part of columnar epithelial cells.

Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Dense irregular connective tissue is present in
questions.solution: Connective tissue is classified as loose connective tissue, dense connective tissue, and specialised connective tissue. Loose connective tissue contains cells and fibers loosely arranged in the matrix. Dense connective tissue contains cells and fibers arranged densely in the matrix. This arrangement can be regular or irregular depending on the orientation of fibers. Dense regular is tendon and ligament depending on whether collagen or elastin is present. Dense irregular is seen in the skin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Common features of striated and faintly striated cardiac muscles are

$\left(a\right)$ Presence of troponin.
$\left(b\right)$ Use of ${Ca}^{2 +}$ for muscle contraction.
$\left(c\right)$ Vascularity
$\left(d\right)$ Gap junctions.
$\left(e\right)$ Control by Visceral Nervous System (ANS).

Which of these features are correct?
questions.solution:
Human muscles are classified into three types depending on location, function and structure. These three types are: $1 )$ Skeletal or striated or voluntary $2 )$ Smooth or involuntary or non striated $3 )$ Cardiac muscles

Cardiac muscles are muscles related to the walls of the heart. These muscles are structurally like skeletal but functionally resemble smooth muscles. These have striations and thus contraction and relaxation results use muscle proteins like troponin , actin , myosin and tropomyosin. Gap junctions are seen in smooth and cardiac muscle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The brood pouch in female cockroach is formed by
questions.solution: In female cockroach, the 7th sternite is largest and boat-shaped. The brood pouch or genital pouch is formed by overlapping of 7th sternite with 8th and 9th sterna, whose anterior part contains female gonopore, spermathecal pores, and collateral glands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
How many structures among the following are lined by squamous epithelium?

a) Inner visceral layer of Bowman's capsule,
b)& Outer parietal layer of Bowman's capsule,
c)& Proximal convoluted tubule,
d)& Thin segment of descending limb of Henle's loop,
e)& Thick segment of ascending limb of Henle's loop,
f)& Distal convoluted tubule, and
g)& Collecting duct.
questions.solution: Nephron consists of Renal corpuscle and Renal tubule. The Renal corpuscle is Bowman's capsule and it has two layers. Inner visceral and outer parietal. Both the layers are made up of squamous epithelium. The renal tubule consists of Proximal convoluted tubule, Distal convoluted tubule, Descending and ascending limbs of loop of henle and collecting duct. Only the descending limb is lined by squamous epithelium. Thus the answer is three.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: With the help of several ommatidia, a cockroach can receive several images of an object. This kind of vision is called:
options: Nocturnal vision, with less sensitivity and less resolution
Mosaic vision, with more sensitivity but less resolution
Mosaic vision, with more resolution but less sensitivity
Nocturnal vision, with more sensitivity and more resolution
questions.solution: Cockroaches belong to phylum Arthropods. The body is divisible into Head, Thorax and Abdomen. Head contains eyes, antennae and mouthparts. There are two pairs of eyes seen in cockroaches : Compound and simple eyes. Compound eyes contain small structures known as Ommatidia and each ommatidium has one lens. There are around 2000 ommatidium in each eye of cockroaches.This forms a Mosaic vision. This vision helps in forming many images of an object and thus helps in alertness of the insect and thus is more sensitive. Since ommatidia are very small structures the image which is formed is of less resolution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Find the statement which is INCORRECT about brown adipose tissue.
options: It is reddish-brown in colour due to more myoglobin.
It is present in developing foetus and newborn.
It is a good insulator and major source of energy reserve.
It is a type of loose connective tissue.
questions.solution: Adipose tissue is a type of Connective tissue. It is specifically loose connective tissue as it shows presence of matrix in which the cells and fibres are loosely arranged. It is the fat storing tissue. It is of two types: White and Brown adipose tissue. In white, there is a single large fat droplet in the cells surrounded by little cytoplasm. The brown fat has many small droplets of fat suspended in large amount of cytoplasm. Brown fat is present in new-born babies and hibernating mammals and it has large tendency to produce heat. The colour is brown due to presence of iron containing pigments and not due to muscle protein i.e. myoglobin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following can be related to the tissue called blood?
options: It has a fibre-free matrix but rich in collagen protein
It has both nucleated and non-nucleated cells, performing aerobic respiration
Blood is a specialised connective tissue
It is a form of dense connective tissue, having dense arrangement due to large count of RBCs
questions.solution: Connective tissue is the most abundant tissue in animals. This tissue is further divided into three types: Loose connective tissue, dense connective tissue, and specialized connective tissue. Loose connective tissue shows a matrix with cells and fibers. These are areolar and adipose tissue. Dense connective tissues are tendons and ligaments. These are known as dense as fibers and cells are densely packed in the matrix. Specialized connective tissues are fluid connective tissues or supporting connective tissues. Fluid connective tissues are blood and lymph as these are fluid and thus fibres are absent. Supporting connective tissues include bone and cartilage as these have lacunae.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement regarding the cockroach.
options: In females, the 7^{th} sternum is boat-shaped.
Males bear a pair of short, threadlike anal styles which are absent in females.
In both sexes, the 9^{th} segment bears a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci.
The abdomen in both males and females consists of 10 segments.
questions.solution: The abdomen in both males and females consists of 10 segments. In females, the 7^{th} sternum is boat shaped and together with the 8^{th} and 9^{th&}sterna forms a brood or genital pouch whose anterior part contains female gonopore, spermathecal pores and collateral glands. In males, genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of abdomen bounded dorsally by 9^{th} and 10^{th} terga and ventrally by the 9^{th} sternum. It contains dorsal anus, ventral male genital pore and gonapophysis. Males bear a pair of short, threadlike anal styles which are absent in females. In both sexes, the 10^{th} segment bears a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the following columns.
&

(1) Skeletal muscles (P) Part of the dark band
(2) Z line (Q) Autonomic nervous system
(3) Henson's zone (R) Syncytial
(4) Visceral muscles (S) Seen in the light band
questions.solution: Skeletal muscles are muscles related to skeletal system of the body. These are voluntary in nature. These are also known as striated muscles due to presence of striations i.e. Dark and Light bands. These muscles are made up of many muscle fibres that contain many myofibrils. These contain many units known as sarcomeres which are the main unit of muscle contraction. Sarcomere extends between two Z lines or krause's membrane. I bands or Isotrophic bands or Light bands are bisected by these Z lines and A bands or Anisotrophic or Dark bands lie in the centre. Hensons zone or H zone is seen traversing the dark bands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The CORRECT statements about the digestive system of cockroach are,

I. The entire foregut of the cockroach is lined by the cuticle.

II. The midgut is broader than the hindgut of the cockroach.

III. The proventriculus of the cockroach has teeth for grinding food particles.

IV. The digestive juice is secreted by 100-150 hepatic caeca present at the junction of foregut and midgut.
questions.solution: The alimentary canal of cockroaches is divided into three regions, namely the foregut, midgut and the hindgut. The foregut has a thick layer of cuticle lying inside the outer layer of circular muscles. The midgut is not as broad as compared to the hindgut and the proventriculus (the expansion of the esophagus above the stomach) has chitinous plates (teeth) for grinding the food particles. The hindgut& is broader than midgut and is differentiated into illeum, colon, rectum. The junction of the foregut and the midgut shows the presence of Malpighian tubules which help in excretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The complex tissues are made up of
options: more than one type of cell
questions.solution: The complex tissue is made up of more than one type of cell. These cells differ from one another in their form and structure; however, these cells work together as a unit. Hence a complex tissue can be defined as a collection of structurally dissimilar cells performing a common function or set of functions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which statement is correct regarding the epithelia of small intestine and PCT?
options: Both are having compund columnar epithelia with microvilli
Both are having stratified columnar epithelial cells
Both are having simple epithelia with microvilli
Both are having stratified epithelia but cells are of different shapes.
questions.solution: Simple epithelia are found in the lining of the small intestine (simple columnar epithelium with brush border) and PCT (simple cuboidal epithelium with brush border).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: In each segment, the exoskeleton has hardened plates called sclerites, sternites dorsally and tergites& ventrally.
The entire body is covered by a hard chitinous exoskeleton (brown in colour).
Head is triangular in shape and lies anteriorly at right angles to the longitudinal body axis.
A pair of thread-like antennae arise from membranous sockets lying in front of eyes.
questions.solution: In each segment, the exoskeleton has hardened plates called sclerites& (tergites& dorsally and sternites ventrally) that are joined to each other by& a thin and flexible articular membrane (arthrodial membrane).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The tissue is a group of cells having

$\left(A\right)$ different origin

$\left(B\right)$ same origin

$\left(C\right)$ performs the same function

$\left(D\right)$ absent in plants
questions.solution: All cells are same in origin or mother cell are same and doing similar work and form tissue. The group of similar cells form tissue.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mark the incorrect statement regarding the head of the cockroach.
options: Formed by the fusion of six embryonic segments.
Head bears appendages forming biting and chewing type of mouth parts.
A pair of broad antennae arise from membranous sockets lying in front of eyes.
questions.solution: The head of the cockroach is hypognathous i.e. the lower jaw is longer than the upper jaw.& Head is triangular in shape and lies anteriorly at right angles to the longitudinal body axis. It is formed by the fusion of six segments and shows great mobility in all directions due to the flexible neck. The head capsule bears a pair of compound eyes. A pair of thread-like antennae arise from membranous sockets lying in front of eyes. Antennae have sensory receptors that help in monitoring the environment.& Anterior end of the head bears appendages forming biting and chewing type of mouth parts.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following epithelium lines the moist surface of the buccal cavity?
questions.solution:
The epithelium which lies on the moist surface of the buccal cavity is stratified non-keratinized squamous epithelium. The superficial layer of this tissue is made up of squamous cells, whereas the underlying layers are made up of cuboidal or columnar cells.

Pseudostratified non-keratinized squamous epithelium is found in the lining of the vas deferens and prostate gland.

Cuboidal epithelium forms the lining of of the thyroid gland, nephrons, renal tubules, etc.

Stratified columnar epithelium forms the lining of pharynx, conjunctiva, male urethra, etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A ground substance secreted by connective tissue accumulated between cells and fibers is&
questions.solution: These cells also secrete modified polysaccharide, which accumulates between cells and fibers and acts as a matrix.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
How many of the following features belong to skeletal muscles?

I. Striped appearance
II. Voluntary nature
III. Not under the control of CNS
IV. Primarily involved in locomotory actions
questions.solution:
Only Statement III is incorrect.

Characteristics of skeletal muscles

- These are closely associated with the skeletal components of the body.

- These are voluntary muscles.

- These are under the control of the nervous system.

- These are primarily involved in locomotory actions and changes of body postures.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these is a striated muscle but not voluntary?
questions.solution:
Human muscles are classified into three types depending on location, function and structure. These three types are:

$1$ Skeletal or striated or voluntary

$2$ Smooth or involuntary or non striated

$3$ Cardiac muscles

Cardiac muscles are muscles related to the walls of the heart. These muscles are structurally like skeletal but functionally resemble smooth muscles. Thus these muscles have striations but are involuntary. These muscles also show presence of intercalated discs that are typically seen only in this group.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Observe the given diagram of a connective tissue. Identify it. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the given tissue?
options: It is a type of loose areolar tissue.
It is present below the skin as a support framework for epithelium.
Excess of nutrients are converted to fats in this tissue.
questions.solution:
Adipose tissue is another type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialised to store fats. The excess of nutrients which are not used immediately are converted into fats and are stored in this tissue.
Areolar tissue is present beneath the skin. Often it serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibres), macrophages and mast cells.&

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements about animal tissues:

A. The smooth muscle fibres are non-striated, fusiform shape and hold together by cell junctions.
B. Cardiac muscle is structurally similar to smooth muscle and acts similar to skeletal muscle.
C. The skeletal muscle is the only multinucleate and voluntary muscle with alternate light and dark striations.
options: A and B are correct; C is incorrect
A is incorrect; B and C are correct
A and C are correct; B is incorrect
A is correct; B and C are incorrect
questions.solution: The smooth muscle fibres are non-striated, fusiform shape or spindle shape which is held together by cell junctions, bundled together in a connective tissue sheath. Cardiac muscle is structurally similar to skeletal muscle and acts involuntarily similar to smooth muscle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The structure that is present in the 9^{th} abdominal segment of cockroach is?
options: anal style and antennae in female.
questions.solution: In cockroach males, the genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of the abdomen bounded dorsally by the 9^{th} and 10^{th} terga and ventrally by the 9^{th} sternum. It contains a dorsal anus, ventral male genital pore, and gonapophysis. Males bear a pair of short, threadlike anal styles in the& 9^{th} abdominal segment which are absent in females. In both sexes, the 10^{th} segment bears a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The epithelial tissues are characterised by:
options: Tight junction, adhering junction and gap junction.
questions.solution: All cells in the epithelium are held together with little intercellular material. In nearly all animal tissues, specialised junctions provide both structural and functional links between its cells. Three types of cell junctions are found in the epithelium and other tissues. These are called as tight, adhering and gap junctions. Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the correct feature of the muscle fibre given below.
options: Contraction of cells as a unit due to the presence of communication junctions
Fusiform tissue found only in the heart.
Muscles have striations and are& bundled together in a parallel fashion.
A sheath of tough connective tissue encloses several bundles of the muscle fibres.
questions.solution: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together. Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit, i.e., when one cell receives a signal to contract, its neighbours are also stimulated to contract.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In cockroach, fore wings are known as:
questions.solution:
Cockroaches are a type of insect belonging to the phylum Arthropoda and these are dioecious.
The first pair of wings arises from mesothorax and the second pair from metathorax. Forewings (mesothoracic) called tegmina are opaque dark and leathery and cover the hind wings when at rest. The hind wings are transparent, membranous and are used in flight.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The mucosal lining of which organ differs from others in concern with the number of layer of the cell (simple/stratified):
questions.solution: Simple epithelia are found in the lining of the stomach (simple columnar epithelium without brush border), small intestine (simple columnar epithelium with brush border) and PCT (simple cuboidal epithelium with brush border).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mouth parts of cockroach are:
questions.solution: Mouth parts in cockroach: These are biting and chewing type. These consist of labrum (upper lip), labium (lower lip), maxillae, mandibles and hypophyarnx (median flexible lobe acting as tongue). A salivary duct opens at the base of the hypopharynx.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following structure is not made up of a single layer of flattened cell with irregular boundaries?
questions.solution: The type of epithelium which is made up of a single layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries is known as squamous epithelium. It forms the endothelium of blood vessels and the lining of alveoli and Bowman's capsule. The type of epithelium which covers the dry surface of the skin is compound epithelium. It is made up of more than one layer of cells. It is protective in function.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: The male reproductive system consists of a pair of testes one lying on each lateral side in the 4^{th}-6^{th} abdominal segments.& The female reproductive system consists of two large ovaries, lying laterally in the 2^{nd}–6^{th} abdominal segments. Anal style is a paired structure present in males in the 9^{th} abdominal segment.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following features is not related to the cockroach?
options: Body divisible into head, thorax and abdomen
Two pairs of wings are found
Three pairs of jointed legs are present on abdomen
Presence of anal cerci in both sexes.
questions.solution:
Thorax of Cockroach is made up of 3 segments - prothorax, mesothorax and metathorax. Neck is the anterior extension of prothorax. Thorax bears the following structures:

A. Legs -1 pair of jointed legs are found in each thoracic segment (6 in number - hexapod).

B. Wings -2 pairs of wings are found :1 pair of mesothoracic wings or tegmina (dark coloured, opaque and leathery, meant for covering of hindwings when at rest) and 1 pair of metathoracic wings (thin, membranous and true wings for flying).
